sources.title: PostgreSQL SELECT locking clause
sources.finding: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED can avoid lock contention for multiple consumers of a queue-like table, but it gives an inconsistent view and therefore needs deterministic ordering and a bounded technical claim/lease transaction rather than general-query use.

sources.title: EF Core ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete
sources.finding: ExecuteUpdate returns the affected-row count, which can implement an explicit conditional transition when a generic durable-work lease, completion, release, or inbox deduplication record must detect a concurrent change.

sources.title: PostgreSQL INSERT
sources.finding: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT supports an atomic unique-key arbiter for a leased inbox reservation, avoiding a check-then-insert race while leaving owner-domain processing outside this capability.

decision: Use PostgreSQL as the durable technical authority for generic durable-work lease/reclaim, retry-eligibility, and consumer-inbox idempotency mechanics. Any claiming query must preserve deterministic ordering and concurrency safety. Caller/owner domains supply the durable work identity, payload meaning, retry policy values, and business effects; RabbitMQ remains transport only.
limitations: This evidence does not authorize domain work types, handler dispatch, timer meaning, retry duration/backoff values, redrive policy, queue configuration, consumer registration, Product event contracts, or any business mutation.

The primary sources support bounded technical concurrency mechanics only. Exact SQL and schema remain subject to authority-backed implementation, migration, focused deterministic tests, and the P1-007 specialist reviews.
No Product, Connected Product, provider, identity, financial, compliance, public API, SDK, runtime configuration, credential, fixed host/port, deployment, or release behavior is authorized.
